nodes.label: The Second Consumer Group
nodes.rationale: This is the point of Phase 3, more than the bars are: Phase 2 shipped exactly one consumer, which is the condition ADR-0001's own 'revisit when' clause names as the point at which the broker stops being justified. A live run shows processor-persist at lag 20 while bar-aggregator replays from 160,736 behind — neither notices the other.

nodes.label: Two Watermarks (Per-Symbol and Global)
nodes.rationale: The global watermark decides when a bar is closed and written; the per-symbol watermark decides when that symbol's bars are sealed. Closing on the global watermark stops a symbol trading once an hour from holding a bar open. Sealing on it destroys data — the first live replay dropped 153,128 trades, because Kafka orders a partition and not a topic. The asymmetry is the whole rule: closing early is harmless, sealing early is not.

nodes.label: Corrections and the Bounded Lateness Window
nodes.rationale: A bar is written the moment its minute ends rather than held for the grace period, because a downstream consumer waiting for a bar should not also wait out a window that exists for a rare case. A bar that can be revised forever is a bar nothing downstream can ever act on. Limitation: a bar reopened from the database cannot place its late trade among trades it no longer holds, so open and close are left alone rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Aggregator Restart Recovery
nodes.rationale: The in-progress bar is written on every flush with is_final=false and offsets are committed only afterwards. Resuming an unfinished bar is not a correction and does not bump revision — announcing a correction that never happened would mislead every consumer watching revision to detect rewritten history.

nodes.label: The Bar Replacement That Would Have Been Silent
nodes.rationale: A trade for a bar the process has no memory of must read the bar from the store and correct it. Without that, a fresh single-trade bar at revision 0 would satisfy `revision <= excluded.revision` and replace a correct bar, with the only evidence being a wrong volume figure.

nodes.label: VWAP Exact for 1m, Null for Rollups
nodes.rationale: Averaging five VWAPs is not a VWAP, and writing a number that looks right would be worse than writing nothing.

nodes.label: SQL Rollups to 5m/1h/1d
nodes.rationale: Derived from stored 1m bars, never from a second pass over trades: two independent paths to the same number is two chances to disagree, and the disagreement would surface as a backtest nobody can reproduce. Open and close are not min and max; bucket boundaries are anchored at the Unix epoch in both the aggregator and the SQL so the two agree.

nodes.label: tradewatch-backfill Job
nodes.rationale: Writes nothing to Kafka: backfilled bars are not market events, and publishing them would drive the aggregator's watermark backwards through history and seal every live bar behind it. History is loaded; events are streamed. Chunked a day at a time so a crash costs a window rather than the job and leaves it empty rather than half-filled.

nodes.label: Resume Only From a Prefix
nodes.rationale: The resume point comes from the data, not a job table, because a job table is a second statement about what has been fetched and the interesting question becomes which is right when they disagree. 'Resume after the newest stored bar' looks equivalent and was wrong in production: a few hours of recent bars made a month-long request resume from today. So resume only when the oldest bar in range sits at its beginning; being wrong in the cautious direction costs an idempotent re-fetch.

nodes.label: Data Quality Checks
nodes.rationale: Invariants are verified, not enforced — the CHECK constraints and NewBar already enforce them, so a non-empty result means something wrote around both layers. Gaps are reported, not judged: a checker that reports every weekend as an outage is a checker people switch off. The session calendar is deliberately holiday-free because an unlisted holiday shows up as a gap an operator recognises, which beats a half-correct table silently hiding a real outage.
